chapters.summary: After inquiring of the LORD, the tribe of Judah leads the attack against the Canaanites, and though they win many victories, they fail to fully drive out the inhabitants of the land, leaving trouble for the future.
keyPoints: Judah and Simeon join forces to defeat the Canaanites, capturing Adoni-bezek and cutting off his thumbs and big toes.
Othniel captures Kiriath-sepher and receives Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife, along with springs of water as a dowry.
The tribes fail to fully drive out the Canaanites, who become a lasting snare to Israel.
chapters.application: We should obey God fully rather than settle for partial victories, for sin left unaddressed brings lasting trouble. Let us ask the Lord for hearts of complete obedience.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how Israel is punished for breaking their covenant with God, and how, after Joshua's death, a new generation forsakes him, marking the beginning of the vicious cycle of the judges era.
keyPoints: God rebukes Israel for not tearing down the pagan altars, which becomes a snare to them.
After Joshua and his generation die, the new generation does not know the LORD and does what is evil in his sight.
God raises up judges to save them, but they still refuse to listen, turning to worship other gods and provoking God's anger.
chapters.application: Let us always remember what God has done and pass our faith on to the next generation, guarding against drifting from him into worldliness, and turn back quickly from rebellion to experience his mercy and deliverance.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how God tests Israel by leaving the Canaanites in the land, and how the judges Othniel, Ehud, and Shamgar deliver Israel.
keyPoints: God leaves the Canaanite nations in the land to test whether Israel will obey his commandments.
Othniel is raised up, defeats Cushan-rishathaim, and the land has peace for forty years.
Ehud assassinates Eglon, king of Moab, and leads Israel to defeat the Moabites.
chapters.application: In times of ease we easily drift from God. Let us ask the Lord for watchful hearts, staying in his word and prayer, relying on the Spirit's power to overcome temptation and live holy lives.

chapters.summary: Because Israel does evil, they are oppressed by the king of Canaan, and the prophetess Deborah, together with Barak, leads the army to defeat the Canaanite commander Sisera.
keyPoints: Israel again does evil, and the LORD hands them over to Jabin, king of Canaan, who oppresses them for twenty years.
The prophetess Deborah summons Barak to battle at God's command; Barak insists that Deborah go with him, and she prophesies that the victory will belong to a woman.
God routs Sisera in defeat, and Jael kills him by driving a tent peg through his head, so that Israel subdues the king of Canaan.
chapters.application: When facing hardship, let us be like Deborah—bravely obeying God's call and trusting that he will grant victory, without fear of our circumstances.

chapters.summary: Deborah and Barak sing a song of victory, praising God for fighting on Israel's behalf and commemorating Jael's killing of Sisera.
keyPoints: Deborah and Barak sing praise to God, recalling how he led Israel to victory.
The song describes God's coming down, the earth shaking, and Israel regaining its freedom.
It commemorates Jael's courage in killing Sisera, making her a hero of the nation.
chapters.application: When God grants victory, let us give thanks through song; and in hardship, let us trust his power and act with courage.

chapters.summary: Gideon is called by God, tears down the altar of Baal, and tests God's will with a fleece as he prepares to lead Israel against the Midianites.
keyPoints: Because Israel does evil, they are handed over to the Midianites and reduced to great misery.
God calls Gideon, promising to be with him and to give him strength to save Israel.
Gideon tears down the altar of Baal, offers a sacrifice to God, and twice tests God's will with a fleece.
chapters.application: When circumstances are difficult, let us trust that God is still with us, respond bravely to his call, and patiently seek his will, letting our actions bear witness to our faith.

chapters.summary: Following God's instructions, Gideon reduces his army to three hundred men and, with trumpets, empty jars, and torches, launches a surprise attack on the Midianite camp and returns victorious.
keyPoints: Through two rounds of testing by how the men drink water, God narrows the army down to three hundred, showing that victory depends on him, not on numbers.
Gideon sneaks down to the enemy camp at night, overhears a dream being told, and his faith is strengthened as he becomes certain that God has already granted the victory.
The three hundred men blow trumpets, smash jars, hold up torches, and shout, throwing the enemy into panic so that they turn on each other.
chapters.application: When our strength is small, let us not be afraid, for God's power is made perfect in weakness. Obey his leading and act in faith, and he will fight for you and give you victory beyond measure.

chapters.summary: Gideon pursues the two kings of Midian, wisely calms the complaints of the men of Ephraim, but ultimately makes a golden ephod that becomes a snare to Israel.
keyPoints: Gideon calms Ephraim's anger with a gentle answer, showing humility and wisdom.
Gideon holds Succoth and Peniel accountable for their indifference, demonstrating justice and perseverance.
Gideon makes a golden ephod, which Israel comes to worship, becoming a snare for the future.
chapters.application: In success and victory, let us guard against pride and drifting from God, keeping him at the center of all things, so that our gifts and achievements never become idols.

chapters.summary: Gideon's son Abimelech schemes to kill his brothers and makes himself king, but he is finally destroyed through the treachery of the men of Shechem and God's judgment.
keyPoints: Abimelech incites the men of Shechem and hires reckless men with silver to kill Gideon's seventy sons.
Jotham tells the parable of the trees and the bramble, foretelling the mutual destruction of Abimelech and the men of Shechem.
Abimelech captures Shechem, but at Thebez a woman drops a millstone on his head and kills him, fulfilling God's judgment.
chapters.application: Let us guard against ambition and pride, acting with humility, for God judges justly, and the wicked will finally come to ruin.

chapters.summary: Israel does evil again, and God punishes them through the Ammonites; when they repent and cry out, God raises up Jephthah as their leader.
keyPoints: Tola and Jair serve as judges, and then Israel again does what is evil in the LORD's sight.
God hands Israel over to the Philistines and the Ammonites, and they suffer for eighteen years.
Israel cries out to God, who reminds them how often they have forsaken him, but in the end he has compassion on them.
chapters.application: We often suffer for our rebellion, yet God is still willing to hear our repentant cries. Let us turn from evil and rely on him wholeheartedly, and he will grant deliverance and peace.

chapters.summary: Jephthah is made leader because of his trust in God and defeats the Ammonites, but his rash vow costs him his only daughter.
keyPoints: Jephthah is made leader of Gilead because God is with him.
Jephthah first reasons with the Ammonites, then defeats them through the power of the Spirit.
Jephthah makes a rash vow, which results in his daughter being dedicated to God for life.
chapters.application: Before making major decisions, let us weigh our words and actions carefully and avoid rash vows; trust in God, and he will guide us in the right path.

chapters.summary: Jephthah the Gileadite defeats the Ephraimites, and after him Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon serve in turn as judges of Israel.
keyPoints: The Ephraimites are angered at not being called to join the battle and clash with the Gileadites.
The Gileadites seize the fords of the Jordan and use a pronunciation test to identify and kill the Ephraimites.
Jephthah judges Israel for six years, and after his death Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon govern in succession.
chapters.application: Let us avoid the division that pride and jealousy bring, resolving misunderstandings through humility and honest communication, and cherishing unity.

chapters.summary: Israel does evil again, and the LORD sends an angel to announce Samson's birth to Manoah and his wife, giving them instructions for raising him as a Nazirite.
keyPoints: Israel again does what is evil in the LORD's sight and is handed over to the Philistines for forty years.
The angel of the LORD appears to Manoah's wife, telling her she will bear a son who must keep the rules of the Nazirite vow.
Manoah prays for the angel to appear again, and after he repeats the instructions, Manoah offers a sacrifice and realizes he has seen the angel of the LORD.
chapters.application: God cares for his people even in hardship. Let us watch for his guidance in ordinary life and be willing to set ourselves apart in obedience to his will.

chapters.summary: Samson goes down to Timnah and, against the law, insists on marrying a Philistine woman—yet God uses it as an opportunity against the Philistines; along the way Samson kills a lion, and at his wedding feast a riddle sparks a conflict.
keyPoints: Samson ignores his parents' objections and insists on marrying the Philistine woman, revealing his willfulness.
Samson tears a lion apart with his bare hands, empowered by the Spirit with superhuman strength.
Samson sets a riddle as a wager, and when his wife betrays the answer, he becomes enraged and kills thirty men.
chapters.application: God can accomplish his purposes even through choices that seem wrong to us, yet we should still guard ourselves carefully, so that our own desires do not lead us into trouble.

chapters.summary: Samson takes revenge on the Philistines after his wife is given to another, burning their crops with torches and later killing many of them; when he grows desperately thirsty, he cries out to God, who causes a spring to burst forth.
keyPoints: When his wife is taken from him, Samson ties torches to foxes and burns up the Philistines' crops.
The Philistines retaliate, and Samson kills a thousand of them with the jawbone of a donkey, displaying God's mighty power.
Samson, overcome with thirst, cries out to God, who makes water gush out, showing his provision and mercy.
chapters.application: When we face injustice, let us, like Samson in his distress, cry out to God, trusting that he will care for us—his grace is sufficient, and his strength is made perfect in weakness.

chapters.summary: Samson, infatuated with the Philistine woman Delilah, betrays the secret of his strength; he is captured and blinded, but after turning back to God in repentance, he dies together with his enemies.
keyPoints: Samson visits a prostitute in Gaza but still manages to escape, showing that God is still with him.
Delilah tests Samson three times without success, but he finally gives away his secret because of his infatuation with her.
After his hair is cut, Samson loses his strength, but as it grows back, he prays to God, has his strength restored, and dies together with his enemies.
chapters.application: When we fall in weakness, let us be like Samson—turning back and crying out to God in our suffering, for he will hear us and grant strength to overcome our hardship.

chapters.summary: Judges 17 records how Micah of Ephraim sets up his own idols and priest, reflecting how, in a time when Israel had no king, everyone did as they saw fit.
keyPoints: Micah steals silver from his mother, and after confessing, she blesses him and uses the silver to make an idol.
Micah sets up a shrine, makes an ephod and household gods, and installs his own son as priest.
A Levite comes to Micah's house, and Micah hires him as priest, believing this will bring the LORD's blessing.
chapters.application: Without clear standards, it is easy to act on our own judgment. Let us ask the Lord for clarity of heart, guided by his word rather than our own opinions, in every decision we make.

chapters.summary: The tribe of Dan sends men to search for territory, takes Micah's idols and priest along the way, and finally conquers Laish, setting up idol worship there.
keyPoints: Having received no territory yet, the tribe of Dan sends men to scout out land to settle.
The Danites take Micah's idols and ephod for themselves and persuade his Levite to become their priest.
The Danites capture Laish, rename it Dan, and set up idol worship there, turning away from God.
chapters.application: Let us be careful about what we choose to follow, never letting human tradition or material things take God's place, so that we do not lose our spiritual way.

chapters.summary: Judges 19 records the tragic story of a Levite and his concubine, revealing the moral decay and social chaos of that dark period in Israel.
keyPoints: A Levite takes back his unfaithful concubine, and on the journey home they stop for the night in Gibeah, a Benjamite town.
Wicked men of Gibeah surround the house demanding the Levite be handed over; he instead sends out his concubine, who is abused through the night and dies.
The Levite cuts his concubine's body into twelve pieces and sends them throughout Israel, shocking the whole nation and calling them to assemble.
chapters.application: When a society turns away from God, morality collapses. Let us hold fast to holiness, be light in the darkness, and influence those around us with love and justice.

chapters.summary: Israel gathers because of the outrage at Gibeah, and when Benjamin refuses to hand over the guilty men, war breaks out, leaving the tribe of Benjamin nearly destroyed.
keyPoints: All the assembly of Israel gathers at Mizpah, demanding that Benjamin hand over the wicked men of Gibeah.
Benjamin refuses and instead musters for battle, defeating Israel twice.
Israel inquires of God and, on the third attempt, defeats Benjamin with an ambush, leaving only six hundred men alive.
chapters.application: When facing sin, let us seek God's guidance rather than act out of raw emotion. In conflict, let us uphold justice while also showing mercy, seeking to restore those who are lost.

chapters.summary: Israel mourns over the near destruction of the tribe of Benjamin and finds a way to provide wives for its surviving men, so that the tribe might be preserved.
keyPoints: Israel had sworn at Mizpah not to give their daughters in marriage to Benjamin, leaving the tribe on the verge of extinction.
When they discover that the people of Jabesh-gilead had not joined the assembly, they strike down its men and give the four hundred surviving young women to the Benjamites.
The remaining Benjamites who still need wives seize dancing women from Shiloh, allowing the tribe of Benjamin to survive.
chapters.application: When our decisions cause harm, let us sincerely seek to make things right and rely on God's mercy to restore relationships, rather than acting on our own devices.
